projects.title: Show HN: ReacherX – Open-source Apollo alternative for founders and devs
projects.author: noobships
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Salman. I started ReacherX as a side project in mid 2023 while studying at university, working part-time, and freelancing. I went full-time on it in June 2026. First time sharing something I built on Hacker News ;) ReacherX is an open-source platform for finding the people you're looking for on X/Twitter and LinkedIn. Unlike tools like Apollo, which pull from a static prospect database, ReacherX runs live searches against current data, so results can be very recent, and it's built for people who aren't salespeople and don't want to learn sales jargon or campaign/sequence tooling. Ideal use cases include finding potential customers, market research/validation before building something, and finding ideal candidates when hiring. I built it because even in 2026, finding the right people/network isn't easy. One question always boggled me: why can't I just describe the people I need in plain English and see a list of people along with the actual sources/evidence showing why they are the right match? After three years in this space, I've also come to think this is less of a funnel problem and more of a networking problem, and the space is pretty closed, which is one reason I wanted ReacherX open source. The workflow is roughly: - Describe who you're looking for and why. - The Agent creates ideal profiles and example mock profiles for you to review. - It continuously searches X/Twitter and LinkedIn using generated search queries. - Each person is qualified with an LLM and enriched with supporting sources/activity and other details. - ReacherX only surfaces people with a match score of 70% or higher. - At 90%+, it can generate an outreach plan for review. - DMs, replies, liking/commenting, profiles, voice notes, and media attachments are built in. You can ask the Agent to handle outreach, or do it yourself through the UI. Everything runs through your own account under configurable rate limits. I've tried to keep it conservative to avoid platform flags, but this is an area I'm still refining and take seriously. It has memory and adapts based on search performance and your feedback/preferences. The searches run in the backend, so the browser can be closed. First results usually take around 5 to 30 minutes, and the workflows keep running until plan limits are reached or a backend error stops them. I ran it for 2 to 3 weeks while looking for potential customers. It processed 50,000 people, but only around 300 scored 70% or higher and were surfaced to me. It's an end-to-end TypeScript project using Next.js and Convex. ReacherX uses Convex Agent, Workflows, Workpool, Memory/RAG, etc. Those durable workflows are the backbone of the system. ReacherX is also part of the Convex Open Source program. One thing I'm still thinking hard about is how this architecture will hold up at scale. At a high level it's a continuous loop: generate queries -> search platforms -> qualify/disqualify results with an LLM -> enrich matches -> keep searching. Another challenge has been social-data APIs. Before X introduced Pay Per Use, its API was prohibitively expensive for this kind of product, and even now it can still be costly. Third-party APIs made it possible for me to build this at a much more reasonable cost. ReacherX is currently in beta (v4), so expect some bugs and rough edges. I'm working on it daily. The hosted product is paid and doesn't have a free tier yet. If you don't want to use the hosted version, you can self-host it. I'm also open to contributors and bug reports on GitHub. I'd especially love feedback on the idea, match quality, architecture/scaling approach, and product philosophy. Anything is welcome :) Demo and background links in the first comment.

projects.title: 1. 做了 7 年前端，今年出来独立接活，网站刚上线，顺便聊聊报价和踩过的坑
projects.author: DevYuFeng
projects.summary: 先说明：这篇最后是想接活的，但我不想只丢个链接就跑，所以把这段时间的一些真实想法和报价一起写了。 **背景** 做前端 / 全栈 7 年多，主力 Next.js + TypeScript ，后端和部署也一起做（ Node / Nest / Vercel 这套）。之前在公司带过项目，也断断续续接过私活，现在全职独立。 最近交付的几个： - 加拿大一个医疗预约平台，Next.js + Nest.js ，前台预约 + 多角色管理后台，工期 50 天，客户是群里认识的 - 一个体检预约小程序，Taro + TypeScript ，从需求到上线 22 天 - 一个极简服装品牌的电商官网，Next.js + Framer Motion 三个我认为最容易翻车的地方 1. 需求边界。"做个类似 XX 的网站"这句话，甲方理解是三个页面，我理解是二十个页面加后台。现在我在报价前会把页面清单、状态流转、角色权限一条条列出来，双方确认完才谈钱。这一步很烦，但能省掉后面绝大部分扯皮。 2. 付款节奏。以前吃过"做完再结"的亏，现在一律分阶段：需求确认 → 首版 → 验收，节点到了就结算，不押款。 3. 交付之后。项目往往不是做完就结束，而是做完才开始出问题。所以部署文档、环境变量、数据模型说明我会一起交，尽量保证下一任（或者你之后招的人）能接得住，不至于被我绑住。 **报价，直接写数字，省得互相猜** - 品牌官网 / 营销站 / 落地页：15k 起 - 业务系统 MVP （登录、表单链路、多角色后台）：35k 起 - 长期技术协作：按月 这不是模板价，具体看页面量、交互密度、业务逻辑和内容准备度。复杂项目我会先给一份拆分建议和排期，你拿去比价也没关系。 **什么活我不接** - 预算几千块要做一整套业务系统的。不是看不起，是这个预算下我既做不完也做不好，硬接是互相耽误。 - 需要驻场，或者要反复跟销售汇报进度的。 - 需求完全没想清楚、又不愿意先花一小时梳理的。这种情况建议先做一次付费的方案评审，比直接开做省钱得多。 - 纯品牌视觉设计。基础的界面设计和设计稿还原我能做，但 VI 、插画这类不是我的强项。 **最后** 个人站刚上线： https://www.mayicode.dev/ 案例、服务范围和报价说明都在上面，联系方式在 /contact 。

projects.title: Show HN: Open Source AI Employees
projects.author: DotSauce
projects.summary: Fable 5 scored 99.19% on WebVoyager a few months ago, a be A benchmark is not your logged-in admin panel. Browser use agents are no longer demos. I believe this is a big tipping point. I have been a web developer for most of my career and building with AI agents for nearly four years. Last October I wrote that the missing piece was browser agents reliable enough to leave alone. So I published this open source repo, so everyone can have high quality AI employees. They are, for the most part, agent harness agnostic and can work on any of them. An AI Employee is a folder of plain text routines that covers one business role: SEO, social, sales, support, web dev, ads, launch work, and a chief of staff that reads the other employees' logs. Eight roles, 60 routines, MIT. They run on your own machine through the agent harness you already use, and they drive your own signed-in browser. Two of the big things that make my agents better: - Recursive self improvement reinforcement - Custom trained recipes to get meaningful work done in browser There's also some other neat features and more planned. Like only-when-needed push notifications for Claude Code and other harnesses that support that. I'm also building in community recipe and ecosystem contribution. Agents may discover workflows or tricks for high level tasks and contribute them to all other agent operators. They run a lot of my own business every day now. One example: full meta ad campaigns, content marketing, SEO, backlink building, community management, app development and management. I recommend you start with one that can take on the work you don't want to do. Or replace yourself. Happy to answer any questions.

projects.title: Show HN: Vsqrd – AWS for Biology Experiments
projects.author: misterchocolat
projects.summary: Hi hn. We built VSQRD, which is a place to order and run outsourced preclinical studies. Right now biotechs that outsource studies to CROs (contract research organizations) have to find them manually. That makes it hard to find the right expertise at the right price. But hey it doesn't have to be this way!! We built vsqrd.com, where CROs can list their study offerings and biotechs can compare and order from them directly. We handle the billing and legal work in the background. We’re starting with low-stakes non-GLP work like cell viability assays and basic in vitro testing. Over time we want to support the entire outsourcing chain all the way to clinical work. If you’re a CRO looking to run more studies or a biotech looking to outsource one sign up!

projects.author: SuperDaniel-cn

github.name: SuperDaniel-cn/supply_chain_toolkit
github.description: 供应链工具箱（Supply Chain Toolkit）| 面向采购、PMC 与库存计划员的桌面级离线库存决策工具。

projects.summary: 一款面向实体制造、工贸与零售企业的纯离线桌面级库存决策工具。 用户导入日常的 Excel/CSV 表格，即可在本地完成需求预测、多物料订货量全局运筹求解、呆滞缺货诊断与库存体检。无需配置数据库，不用联网，零 IT 部署成本。 为什么做它？ 中小企业的库存管理常年处于两难：专业 ERP/APS 动辄几十万且实施沉重；日常使用巨型 Excel 动辄卡死闪退，算不准上千物料在总资金预算下的平衡。同时，由于单件采购价格与客户需求属于核心商业机密，企业往往抗拒上传云端 SaaS。 为此，我们用 Tauri + Rust 打造了这款完全运行在本地的高性能小工具。 技术亮点 Tauri v2 + Rust：轻量跨平台原生体验（支持 macOS Apple 芯片 / Win 10/11），运筹算法并行高速求解。 100% 离线与隐私保护：嵌入式 SQLite 本地自闭环，断网完全可用，数据不出个人电脑。 实用业务约束对齐：直接对齐供应商最低订货量 (MOQ) 与最小包装量 (MPQ) 物理约束，算出的建议清单可直接导回 ERP 执行。 费用属性：完全免费、无需注册登录，安装即用。 界面截图

projects.title: Show HN: Ifso.io – Personal finance simulator with no sign up required
projects.author: timer_interrupt
projects.summary: Hey all! I've been building Ifso.io, it's a personal finance simulator that lets you configure and play out life decisions. The main philosophy that I built Ifso around is decision-making. I personally wanted to see what it would look like if I made some key financial decisions (ex: what would it look like if I paid extra on my mortgage principal for just a few years versus putting that money into taxable investments). The existing tools were a bit frustrating however, I felt like I wanted to just tell the simulators "here's what I want to do, how does it end up for me?", but none of the tools really allowed for that. They felt a bit over-complicated for something that I felt should be a bit more straightforward, which is why I ended up building Ifso out. You start off with entering where your finances are right now, and you configure your plan by listing out your various decisions to see how it all plays out and if your financial plan works or not. The list of decisions you can make could include the more obvious things like retiring, buying a home, upgrading your car, etc. You can also simulate what it's like to convert a property into a rental or retiring early and relying on your taxable accounts to carry you to retirement age. I also wanted to make it easy to turn certain "knobs", so if you want to update your income, retirement or investment contributions, extra principal payments, etc, you can easily do so by just updating the contribution numbers for a given year and the simulator carries it forward from that point onwards. Behind the scenes the simulation engine runs through all of the math for you, this includes income taxes, capital gains taxes if you withdraw from a taxable account, retirement account withdrawals, loan amortization schedules (and how extra principal payments might change that), and so on. You can also run Monte Carlo simulations to stress test plans, and create multiple scenarios to compare them side by side. One of the pieces of feedback I'd received is that people wished they could just use it and try it out without needing to sign up. I made the app usable without any sign in, it ends up storing your plan config locally within your browser and is fully usable. If you do want to have your plan persist across devices (or be resilient to any browser resets), you can always sign in for free if you'd like. My goal is to create an easy to use interface, and have all of the complexity be handled for you. To that end, if there's ever any UX improvement I could make or if there's any other features that would be helpful to have, let me know and I'd be happy to look into it!

projects.author: greenzorro

github.name: greenzorro/excel-ps-batch-export
github.description: Python script for reading a PSD template and applying contents in a spreadsheet to export plenty of images. It's an alternative to Photoshop Image > Variables > Define.

projects.summary: 这是一个结合 Excel 数据与 Photoshop 模板的批量出图工具。通过 Python 读取 PSD 模板图层，将电子表格中的文字、图片路径、显示状态自动套入模板批量生成高质量图片。彻底替代 Photoshop 原生「图像 > 变量 > 定义」繁琐的 CSV 导入与批处理流程，适用于电商主图批量制作、证书卡片生成、活动海报自动化等场景。 亮点 1. 免启动 Photoshop GUI：基于 psd-tools 与 Pillow，轻量高效，在服务器或无 PS 桌面环境下亦可批量自动化渲染； 2. 直观的图层命名规则：只需在 PSD 图层名加上 @name#t（文字）、#i（图片替换/九宫格对齐）、#v（可见性），一次配置模板，终身直接贴表格数据即可出图； 3. 支持自动化监控与剪贴板导入：支持监听 Excel 文件变动自动出图，或直接从网页/表格复制数据一键粘贴渲染。
projects.titleZh: [开源推荐] Excel+PS 批量自动出图工具
projects.summaryZh: 结合 Excel 数据与 Photoshop PSD 模板的批量出图工具：基于 psd-tools 与 Pillow，无需启动 Photoshop GUI，读取图层文字、图片路径和显示状态并批量渲染。
projects.summaryEn: Python tool batch-renders images from PSD templates (psd-tools, Pillow), filling text, image paths and visibility from spreadsheets via @name#t/#i/#v layers. Replaces Photoshop variables/CSV; watches Excel changes and clipboard paste.

projects.title: Show HN: Forexfin – Trading calculators, alerts and a journal in one place
projects.author: howtobatman101
projects.summary: Some many years ago I started trading here and there and whenever I was doing it, I was bouncing between different platforms for position sizing, pip value, spread cost etc. Each of them was more or less expensive, I've also met some nice free tools along the way. But. Long story short, I built my own stuff, because first of all, I wanted them in a single place, under my control and by building them, I would be learning something along the way. I'm inviting you to check ForexFin.tech For all my projects I used initially ChatGPT (static stuff), Codex, GitHub's Copilot. Since February I've been relying on Claude an my own research and learnings along the way. It is not a financial advice tool. There's still work to be done and I've got a semi-clear roadmap, but it is just this much you can do as solo dev and this week I'm just going to stop here and present it to the public. If you're having a spin, I would like to kindly ask you to use the "report a bug" button, if your time allows. Suggestions are also welecomed. I usually do follow ups to the reports, but you can write out if you don't want an update. What's in it Calculators: position size, pip value, spread cost, trade plan builder (shareable via URL hash), trade architect with a candle chart Live forex market hours / session overlap, DST- and weekend-aware Currency strength meter (8-currency basket) and a pair correlation matrix with a 14/30/60/90d window Email price alerts across FX, crypto, metals, stocks and ETFs A trading journal that imports broker CSVs (or a screenshot) and reports behavioural stats rather than just P&L Stack (boring, from what I've been told) Node 20 + Express 4, server-rendered HTML SQLite via better-sqlite3, single file, migrations inline and idempotent Frontend is static HTML + one main.css + two small JS files. No framework, no bundler, no build step. FCP budget is under 1s on 4G and it's been easy to hold PM2 + nginx on a single small VPS, Let's Encrypt Market data from Twelve Data, with ECB reference rates as an automatic fallback so a vendor outage degrades instead of breaking Postmark for magic-link sign-in and alert emails. No trackers beyond consent-gated GA4

projects.title: Show HN: Open-source revenue recognition and analytics for Stripe and Metronome
projects.author: tanin
projects.summary: Hi HN, I’m Tanin. For about four years, I worked on the Revenue Recognition and Analytics teams at Stripe. Today, I'm open-sourcing Book of Revenue, a self-hosted revenue engine and drop-in alternative to Stripe Revenue Recognition (with optional support for Metronome). ### The Problem: Most founders track MRR or cash collected in Stripe and assume that reflects revenue. But cash collected isn't revenue, and MRR isn't an accounting metric. Once you hit scale, raise institutional capital, or prep for an audit, ASC 606 / IFRS 15 rules kick in: - Annual upfront subscriptions must be amortized monthly as deferred revenue. - Mid-cycle upgrades, prorations, usage overages, refunds, and disputes quickly turn into messy manual spreadsheets. - Finance and engineering end up arguing because Stripe dashboard numbers never match QuickBooks or NetSuite during month-end close. ### What Book of Revenue Does: - Automated Revenue Recognition: Computes GAAP/IFRS-compliant revenue schedules from your Stripe billing and payment events out of the box. - Unified Financial Truth: Aligns founder analytics with your accountant’s ledger so both sides look at the exact same numbers. - Full Data Ownership: Self-hosted with no vendor lock-in. You retain complete custody of your customer financial records and intermediate data models. ### Looking for Early Users: I’m looking for early design partners—particularly companies processing over $100k in annual volume who dread month-end reconciliations. I'm offering free hands-on deployment and a complimentary audit of your current Stripe/Metronome billing architecture. If you’d like to test it out, drop a comment below or email me directly at tanin@bookofrevenue.com. Website: https://bookofrevenue.com GitHub: https://github.com/tanin47/book-of-revenue

projects.title: Show HN: ReacherX – Open-source platform to find and reach the right people
projects.author: noobships
projects.summary: Hi HN, I'm Salman. I started ReacherX as a side project in mid 2023 while studying at university, working part-time, and freelancing. I went full-time on it in June 2026. First time sharing something I built on Hacker News ;) ReacherX is an open-source platform for finding the people you're looking for on X/Twitter and LinkedIn. There's also an interactive demo linked in the README, prepopulated with fictional data, so you can click around and get a feel for the product without setting anything up. It isn't connected to the real backend. Ideal use cases include finding potential customers, doing market research/validation before building something, and finding ideal candidates when hiring. I built it because even in 2026, finding the right people/network isn't easy. One question always boggled me: why can't I just describe the people I need in plain English and see a list of people along with the actual sources/evidence showing why they are the right match? Existing tools are focused heavily on sales professionals. I am not a salesperson. I don't understand sales jargon. I wanted something that "just works" when I describe who I am looking for. No campaigns or sequences to learn. After spending three years in this space, I also came to realise that this is less of a funnel problem and more of a networking problem. The whole space is also pretty closed, which is one reason I wanted ReacherX open source. The workflow is roughly: - Describe who you're looking for and why. - The Agent creates ideal profiles and example mock profiles for you to review. - It continuously searches X/Twitter and LinkedIn using generated search queries. - Each person is qualified with an LLM and enriched with supporting sources/activity and other details. - ReacherX only surfaces people with a match score of 70% or higher. - At 90%+, it can generate an outreach plan for review. - DMs, replies, liking/commenting, profiles, voice notes, and media attachments are built in. You can ask the Agent to handle outreach, or do it yourself through the UI. You can also upload a product demo and tell the Agent to use it when appropriate. It has memory and adapts based on search performance and your feedback/preferences stored in memory. The searches run in the backend, so the browser can be closed. First results usually take around 5–30 minutes, and the workflows keep running until plan limits are reached or a backend error stops them. ReacherX doesn't rely on an internal static prospect database for discovery. It performs searches against current X/Twitter and LinkedIn data, so results can be very recent. I ran it for 2–3 weeks while looking for potential customers. It processed 50,000 people, but only around 300 scored 70% or higher and were surfaced to me. It's an end-to-end TypeScript project using Next.js and Convex. ReacherX uses Convex Agent, Workflows, Workpool, Memory/RAG, etc. Those durable workflows are the backbone of the system. ReacherX is also part of the Convex Open Source program. One thing I'm still thinking hard about is how this architecture will hold up at scale. At a high level it's a continuous loop: generate queries -> search platforms -> qualify/disqualify results with an LLM -> enrich matches -> keep searching. Another challenge has been social-data APIs. Before X introduced Pay Per Use, its API was prohibitively expensive for this kind of product, and even now it can still be costly. Third-party APIs made it possible for me to build this at a much more reasonable cost. ReacherX is currently in beta (v4). It has bugs and rough edges, and I'm working on it every day. The hosted product is paid and doesn't have a free tier yet. If you don't want to use the hosted version, you can self-host it. I'm also open to contributors and bug reports on GitHub. I'd especially love feedback on the idea, match quality, architecture/scaling approach, and product philosophy. Anything is welcome :)

projects.title: 做了个 TikTok 工具站：不登录就能看，无水印下载，整条评论区能导出 CSV
projects.author: brianbian
projects.summary: 起因是自己做 TikTok 选题调研的时候，老想扒某个号最近在发什么、评论区在吵什么。但登录自己的号去翻有两个问题：一是会进对方的浏览者列表，二是刷着刷着就被推荐流带跑了。市面上的工具要么弹窗套弹窗，要么点「下载」给你一个 APK ，要么评论区只让你看前 20 条。 所以自己做了一个： https://tikviewer.org/ 四个点： 1. 不登录、不装插件。输入用户名或粘贴视频链接就能看，全程不碰你的 TikTok 账号，所以也不会出现在谁的浏览者列表里。 2. 单个视频下载免费，不限次数。无水印的原画质 MP4 、TikTok 自带水印的分享版、只要声音的 MP3 ，三个都有。视频直接走 TikTok 自己的 CDN ，我这边不留副本。 3. 整条评论区能读完，也能带走。导出 CSV / Excel ，字段是内容、作者、作者主页链接、点赞数、回复数、置顶和作者点赞标记、时间。每行带自己的 id 和父 id ，所以随便按哪列排完序，回复挂在哪条评论下面还认得出来。回复是可选的，打开后回复紧跟在评论后面。 4. 整个主页可以批量打包。选前 N 条或者全部，后台跑完给一个 ZIP ，中途关页面也不影响。 也把做不到的说清楚：私密账号进不去（没有任何工具进得去，宣称能进的都是骗你的），已删除和地区限制的视频拿不到，图文帖没有视频可存，「谁看过谁的故事」这种数据也查不到。 商业模式摆在明面上：看和读一直免费，导出和批量下载按量算积分（导出一条评论 1 积分，批量下载一个视频 100–200 积分），注册送 2000 积分够试一圈，订阅年付 5 刀/月起。 欢迎试试，遇到抓不下来的链接欢迎丢过来。

projects.title: Show HN: Jinx – a link shortener you host free on GitHub Pages
projects.author: SubmersibleZoom
projects.summary: Jinx is just links, a small static website on GitHub to share short links to your stuff. Add your links to one file, turn on GitHub Pages, and point your own domain at it. I built it because the options all seemed wrong for a small team: paid shorteners charge monthly for what's essentially a lookup table; free self-hosted ones (YOURLS, Shlink, etc.) still need a server and a database to maintain; and free tiers of hosted services like bitly or tinyurl cap your links or paywall basic features. It’s working well for my team at work. What it does: • Short links on your own domain (yourname.com/thing) that redirect instantly. • A searchable page listing all your links. Typos are redirected to the search page. • QR codes for each link, generated in js in the browser, no external API calls. • Click counts via GoatCounter (free, privacy-preserving, no cookies) • Nested paths if you want them (e.g. contact/email, contact/whatsapp, etc.) • Access control for who can edit links is done through github repo access. Why another link shortener? Paid link shorteners cost money every month for something that's really just a lookup table. Free open-source link shorteners require you to host the app somewhere and pay monthly for that instead. Freemium services like bitly paywall you with limits on the number of links, edit ability, sometimes redirect your QR code to an ad . So I built a link shortening tool focused on simplicity as a static website and open-sourced it. Setup: fork the repo, edit the config and the links, turn on GitHub Pages. Takes about five minutes. MIT licensed, free, no ads, no account required beyond GitHub itself. Live example: jinx.fyi Code: github.com/gdmcdonald/jinx Would love to hear feedback, what do you like or not like, what would make it more useful for you?

projects.title: Show HN: Nexus-Arc – pay-per-call and job escrow for AI agents on Arc
projects.author: irfndi
projects.summary: Hi HN — I built Nexus-Arc. AI agents can call APIs and run multi-step work, but they still cannot open a Stripe account or hold a corporate card. Prepaid credits lock capital; L1 fees make $0.001 calls uneconomic; L2 batch latency breaks tight loops. Nexus-Arc is a dual-rail gateway live on Arc mainnet (chain 5042), where USDC is native gas: 1. Synchronous rail — HTTP 402 / x402. Agent hits an endpoint unsigned, gets a 402 + challenge, signs a Permit2 / EIP-712 voucher, retries with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE. Settlement is in-process, sub-second, pay-per-call. No API keys. 2. Asynchronous rail — ERC-8183 escrow (NexusJobs). Client locks a USDC budget, provider submits a deliverable hash (IPFS/Arweave), evaluator releases payout. State machine: Open → Funded → Submitted → Terminal. Expiry refunds the client. Live screener (expect HTTP 402 on an unpaid GET): https://nexus-arc.pryx.dev/v1/screener Explorer: https://explorer.arc.io Stack is Bun + Effect TS on Arc. Fees are small (x402 ~0.1% + $0.0005; escrow 75 bps on completion). Happy to answer questions on the 402 self-facilitation path, Permit2 vouchers, or the escrow evaluator. What should I wire next — MCP tools, more paid APIs, or agent identity (ERC-8004)?

projects.summaryZh: AI Agent 双轨支付网关：x402 按次付费 + ERC-8183 任务托管结算，Arc 主网，USDC 原生 gas，无需 API Key。

projects.title: Show HN: Vending Machine Lab – Build business, leave for 2 wks, see what breaks
projects.author: professorgc
projects.summary: I spent a while exploring whether AI could help build businesses that operate with little ongoing owner involvement. This was inspired in part by Andon Labs’ Vending-Bench work on AI agents running simulated businesses. Their Project Vend collaboration with Anthropic takes that question into a real shop. (Obviously it was also inspired by "the dream.") Unfortunately, currently, I think the answer is generally "no." Vending-Bench shows outcomes relative to a well-defined business environment, while starting businesses isn't well-defined and much harder, for us and AI. But one useful result was this browser simulation, which I'm sharing as a free side project. It basically generalizes the idea behind Vending-Bench itself, but in a simulation that anyone can mess around with, including AI. Choose a digital product, custom digital service, vending machine, or reusable equipment such as a laundromat. Set demand, costs, staffing and rules, then run 14 simulated days without the owner. Inspect unfinished orders, cash, refunds and requests for your help. Change the setup and rerun the same conditions. The model supplies fictional customers and failures. AI help has preset outcomes; no model is called by the site. It's a way to explore operating assumptions, not a demand or profit forecast. An optional copy/paste workflow lets your own assistant plan decisions with the fictional fortnight known in advance. It is not thinking live between days. I developed it with substantial AI coding assistance, automated checks, AI role-playing of users (occupying user types/roles), and feedback from human friends who tried it. It runs in the browser without signup. Repo here: https://github.com/automatedteach/vending-machine-lab

projects.title: Show HN: Give your AI agents access to WhatsApp
projects.author: fabian_shipamax
projects.summary: Hi, I built Chat-Man because I wanted a cheap way to give my agents access to WhatsApp without integrating a WhatsApp library separately in every project. You get WhatsApp MCP server, so you can connect WhatsApp to an agent and programmatically read, search, extract and send messages - but also have a web UI for non-techies. You can also receive webhooks for incoming messages for starred conversations. What you can do with the MCP? -Read WhatsApp messages and turn them into CRM records -Summarise conversations or groups -Extract structured information from messages -Find messages, participants or other WhatsApp data -Send messages -Manage group memberships Of course.. you always need to follow data protection regulation. The web UI: -Edit group details -See who joined or left -See who is most active -Export group members -Match members against a CSV (e.g. from a CRM) -Bulk message members -Bulk kick members -Create invite links For individual contacts, you can send messages directly from the UI. Why I built it for myself? I needed WhatsApp access for several projects (hermo.ai, florahaus.co.uk, …) and didn't want to pay for a WhatsApp integration for each project. Link: https://chat-man.net I’d love to get some feedback, especially from people building agents that need access to WhatsApp. Fabian

projects.summary: 找工作最熬人的不是面试，是在几个招聘网站上重复点「投递」。这个项目用浏览器自动化接管了这一步：配好岗位、城市、薪资范围，它会在 Boss 直聘等平台自动筛选投递，跳过不活跃的 HR 和猎头岗位，结果通过企业微信推给你。全程有网页界面，不用改代码。 亮点 1. 真的接了大模型：先算岗位和简历的匹配度，再按 JD 现写一条打招呼语，不是模板群发。 2. 自动发图片简历：打完招呼直接把简历发过去，不用干等 HR 开口要，回复率明显更高。 3. 自动维护黑名单：发过「不合适」的 HR，他们公司会进黑名单，不重复骚扰同一家。 4. 对学习者有参考价值：用 Patchright（Playwright 的反检测分支）应付真实网站的风控，比教程里的 demo 实在得多；后端 Spring Boot 3.5 + SQLite，前端 Next.js 16 + React 19，是一套完整可跑的现代 Java 全栈项目。

projects.title: 【工具自荐】AnonPeek：不用登录，快速查看 Instagram 公开资料
projects.author: melodyxian
projects.summary: AnonPeek 最近做了一个比较轻量的 Instagram 公开资料查看工具，叫 AnonPeek。 有时候只是想快速确认一个 Instagram 账号，看看用户名、简介、粉丝数量或者最近发布的公开内容，但为了这么简单的查询还需要登录账号，整个过程会比较麻烦。 所以做了 AnonPeek，希望把这个过程变得简单一点。 使用时只需要输入 Instagram 用户名，或者直接粘贴公开的 Instagram 个人主页链接，就可以查看整理后的公开资料。网站不要求登录 Instagram 账号。 目前可以查看的信息包括： 用户名和显示名称 个人简介 头像和公开主页链接 Followers、Following、Posts 等公开数据 可获取的公开照片、视频和 Carousel 帖子 caption 以及对应的原始链接 在有可用公开媒体地址时，可以打开或下载相关媒体 我比较重视的一点是，它并不是用来绕过 Instagram 的隐私设置。AnonPeek 只能处理公开账号能够被数据提供方获取的信息，无法查看 private account、Close Friends 或其他受限制的内容。 我觉得它比较适合做一些简单的账号查询，比如品牌做竞品或市场调研、寻找创作者、联系之前先确认账号信息，或者只是想快速查看一个公开 Instagram 主页。 另外，网站采用短期缓存来减少重复请求，并不会提供永久的个人搜索历史功能。由于公开数据本身可能受到账号改名、删除、地区限制、缓存和数据提供方限制影响，所以重要信息还是建议回到 Instagram 原始页面确认。 如果你平时只是偶尔需要查看 Instagram 的公开资料，又不想为了简单查询专门登录账号，可以试试 AnonPeek。

projects.title: 【开源自荐】My Portfolio：本地优先的个人资产管理，数据只在你浏览器里，默认一季度才更新行情
projects.author: CDz1129

github.name: CDz1129/my-portfolio
github.description: portfolio 展示工具

projects.summary: APP URL： 一句话简介：一个本地优先的个人资产记录与展示工具——数据只存在你自己的浏览器里，永不离开本地。 自荐正文： 做这个的起点很朴素：我想要一个地方能一眼看清自己的资产，但市面上的同类 App 大多需要付费，而且价格不低，于是干脆自己动手做一个。 它想解决的是：把散落在各个账户里的东西——现金、投资（A 股 / 港股 / 美股 / 加密货币）、固定资产、应收款、负债——集中到一处，看清净资产、资产配置和净值走势。 核心卖点只有一个：数据只存在你自己的浏览器（IndexedDB）里，不会上传到任何服务器。 没有账号、没有登录、没有云端数据库、没有统计。行情服务只是一个无状态代理，只转发公开的股价 / 汇率请求，服务器不保存任何用户数据。代价也很直白：换一个浏览器，数据就不在了，所以内置了完整的 JSON 备份与恢复。 几个我自己比较在意的设计： 1. 默认每季度才更新一次行情，而不是实时。 听说每秒盯盘的、每天看盘的、一年看一次的，长期结果往往不一样，常常是后一种更从容。我希望这个工具里的资产都是能让人安心睡觉的，一个季度看一次也不会慌，少一点频繁看盘的杂念。（频率可在设置里改，也随时能手动更新。） 2. 两种资产视角：既能按账户类型看配置，也能切到「按流动性」——券商里的现金算流动资产，只有持仓算投资资产。 3. 中英双语，一键切换；总资产的显示货币也能在首页直接切换。 4. 本地优先的工程取舍：用浏览器 IndexedDB 而不是 SQLite，换来零后端、可离线、无原生依赖；账本用事件溯源，账户只存期初余额，其余由流水回放，净值走势可以自由重算。演示数据放在独立数据库，和真实数据完全隔离。 技术栈：React 18 + TypeScript + Vite + Tailwind；Dexie（IndexedDB）做本地存储；Recharts 画图；vite-plugin-pwa 支持 PWA。行情代理在本地用 Node、在云端用 Cloudflare Worker，共用同一份代码。MIT 协议。 它不是生活记账软件：虽然也记录收入 / 支出 / 转账 / 买卖 / 余额调整，但本质是资产盘点与展示，和按笔记录日常开销的记账 App 完全不同。 可以一键部署到 Cloudflare Workers（内置限流与边缘缓存），也可以只跑本地。诚邀试用，欢迎 issue 交流。

github.description: A public board for memes, creative projects and mutual aid. Direct multi-network crypto support with zero platform commission.

projects.author: xinxing870126-prog

github.name: xinxing870126-prog/recruit-os
github.description: Help every interviewer conduct better interviews. AI-assisted preparation, live follow-ups, and evidence-based assessment. Self-hosted. UI currently in Chinese.

projects.summary: 面试聊了一个小时，最后只能写“感觉不错” “表达挺好，项目也做过，感觉可以推进。” 写完这句评价，再问自己：他说的成果，有多少是他本人做的？你认可他的能力，依据是哪段回答？下一轮还需要验证什么？ 我做 Recruit OS，就是希望帮助面试官把这些问题问清楚。目标很直接：让所有的面试官会面试。 这是一个已经在我所在公司实际使用的 AI 辅助面试工作台，现在以 MIT 协议开源，支持企业独立部署。 一个具体例子 在仓库的虚构演示案例中，候选人说：“我们改革了提成方案，年化节省约 220 万。” 工作台为这类回答准备了具体的追问： 说的是“我们”：哪一步由你独立负责？哪个决定是你做的？ 给了一个漂亮数字：测算基线是什么？哪些已经发生，哪些只是全年预测？ 沿着这些问题，面试官可以进一步厘清本人贡献、团队决策、实际结果与预测。 工作台如何辅助面试 面试前：结合岗位、简历和前序面试信息，准备本轮目标、提问路线和验证重点。 面试中：围绕当前话题，结合对话提供追问与参谋建议。 面试后：整理对话证据、风险与未核实的问题，生成反馈草稿，由面试官确认最终结论。 项目还包含岗位管理、候选人分析、面试协作和飞书相关集成。

projects.summaryZh: Recruit OS 是 MIT 协议开源、可自主部署的 AI 面试工作台，帮助面试官把“感觉不错”追问到证据：面试前结合岗位与简历确定目标与验证重点，面试中提供追问与参谋建议，面试后整理证据、风险…

projects.title: Show HN: QuantSupport, a Rust-based quant library
projects.author: jmelo11
projects.summary: Hi, I wanted to share a project I've building for a while. QuantSupport is a quant library that comtemplates curve construction, simulation and risk analytics for a different asset classes (equity, rates, fx, FI). https://github.com/jmelo11/quantsupport It's goal is to be a realistic production tool for financial institutions, instead of being another analytics library as many other tools are. For this, it leverages automatic differentiation from the ground up to obtain risk functionalities (sensitivites), essential for real trading setups. The library features other engines, like and XVA engine and a scripting language for structuring more complex payoff structures. Also, its available an example in the following repo: https://github.com/jmelo11/derivative_structuring where LLMs leverage the scripting functionalities of the library to provide pricing and insights to user prompted requests, allowing model-consitent results and showing the flexibility of the library. I like to think that is reaching a more mature state, but to know for sure, it would be very helpful to get feedback from people from the quant space. Any feedback is highly appreciated.

projects.title: 【工具自荐】货号配图核对台：本地核对CSV清单与商品图片，附试用包
projects.author: tsetwf-cloud
projects.summary: 用 AI 辅助做了一个很小的中文工具，想验证它是否对电商运营、供货图片交接或代上架有用。 场景是手头已有一份货号清单和一批图片，交接前需要检查哪些货号缺图、哪些重复，以及相似货号是否会配错。它只核对文件名、文件夹名和数量，不识别图片内容。 当前能做什么 导入 UTF-8 CSV（货号、所需图片数），再选择图片或货号文件夹。 显示缺图、数量超出、重复货号、同名文件冲突、未匹配和匹配歧义。 导出 CSV 核对报告；确认图片对应关系后，将数量匹配的分组打包为 ZIP，不修改原图。 单个 HTML，无外部脚本依赖，文件在本机浏览器处理，不上传商品资料。 例如清单同时有 A 和 A-B 时，A-B.png 会列为歧义，不自动猜测；0011.png 不会当作货号 001 的图片。 试用 附件包含工具、使用说明、示例清单和合成占位图片。下载并解压后，用桌面浏览器打开 HTML；也可先点击“加载演示”。当前样品免费试用，无需注册工具账号。 目前限制为最多 500 行清单、200 张图片、图片合计 100 MB。支持 JPG/JPEG/PNG/WebP，不支持 XLSX 直接读取、自动识图、图片编辑或自动上架。 已经在当前 Windows 内置浏览器中实测清单/图片/文件夹导入、异常处理、报告及 ZIP 下载，并用独立解压库核验原图字节不变。尚未覆盖所有浏览器版本、手机和极限容量性能。包内示例不是客户资料。 想了解实际工作中的需求 1. 你是否遇到过这类图片交接核对，每周大约处理多少货号？ 2. 现在用 Excel、脚本还是现成软件完成？这份样品缺少哪一步才无法用于实际工作？ 3. 如果以后推出维护完善的版本，一次性 19.9 元是否值得，还是现有免费办法已经足够？这只是价格假设，目前不收款。 欢迎直接在本帖反馈，不需要留下联系方式或上传真实业务资料。测试错误可以用几条虚构货号和文件名说明。 货号配图核对台试用样品.zip

projects.title: [开源] Sirius： LLM 自我驱动的币安 U 本位合约交易机器人（提示词对决策影响非常大）
projects.author: roryzh
projects.summary: https://github.com/heider-x/sirius 币安 U 本位合约，Python 。自己看行情、自己下单、自己调仓、自己补保护单，人只在飞书收成交确认、账户总览和安全告警。 ## 架构思路 就一条：**LLM + TOOLCALLS 的自我驱动**。往下拆四层： ## 1. 决策层（ brain ） 一个有界循环，最多 64 步，调工具、看返回、再调。连续 3 次调同一个工具直接掐断。它唯一的输出是一句话总结和工具调用，没有其他权力。 ## 2. 执行层（ tools ，37 个） 分两类。行情类只读、可并行；下单类串行，且每个写操作里都嵌着硬约束——杠杆上限、保证金模式、单笔名义上限，开仓没有 STOP 直接拒绝并返回结构化错误。LLM 想绕？绕不过，入口就一个。 ## 3. 账本层（ sync ，独立逻辑） 订单/成交/资金费每分钟落库，FIFO 重算，和交易所三路对账。故意和决策层解耦：LLM 全挂，账本照样记，对账照样告警。 ## 4. 调度层（ scheduler ） 通用间隔调度，单任务锁防重叠，单 tick 超时熔断。任务之间只通过 DB 和交易所状态通信，不直接调对方，挂一个不影响其他。 剩下两个都是哨兵思想：保护哨兵常驻 WS ，有成交没保护单就按 2×ATR 补，灰尘 ATR 直接拒绝。 ⚠️ 风险提示：本项目是实盘交易机器人，连接交易所真实 API ，下单即花真钱。请先在测试网 / 小资金上充分验证，再考虑实盘。作者不对任何交易亏损负责。

projects.summary: QuantDinger 是一个开源、自托管的 Python 量化交易工作台，串联市场研究、Strategy API V2 策略开发、历史回测、纸盘交易、实盘执行和监控。项目提供 Docker 部署、公开的策略开发指南、Agent Gateway 和 MCP 服务，适合交易研究员、Python 开发者和希望掌握策略与凭据的个人或小团队。 亮点 策略代码、回测和部署使用同一套 Strategy API V2 工作流。 长时间策略运行由 trading worker 负责，有限回测和研究任务由 Celery 负责，状态进入 PostgreSQL。 MCP 默认使用 stdio，也支持 SSE 和 streamable HTTP；变更操作需要幂等键，实盘权限默认关闭。 后端采用 Apache-2.0；Web 和移动端仓库有单独许可证。

projects.title: 【工具自荐】抖评岛：把抖音公开评论和回复整理成 Excel / CSV
projects.author: kenny-shaw
projects.summary: 我是抖评岛的开发者，想自荐一个做评论整理的小工具。 给一条抖音视频做复盘，或者整理商品反馈时，常常需要把评论交给同事继续看。几张截图能说明一个例子，后面要筛选、加备注、找回某句话的回复，就还是表格方便。 我做的 抖评岛 ExportDou 处理的是这一步：粘贴公开视频分享链接，先看评论预览，再选择要导出的数量、是否包含回复，最后下载 Excel 或 CSV。用户不用安装插件，也不用交出抖音 Cookie。任务在后台运行，可以关掉页面，之后回来取文件。 想先看看表格长什么样，可以直接下载 CSV 样例。里面只有三条编写的示例数据，方便看字段和评论、回复之间的关系。表格拿到手以后，怎么分类、哪些反馈值得跟进，仍然由使用者判断；工具没有自动生成分析结论。 如果需要把这一步接到自己的工作流里，也有 API、CLI 和 Agent Skill 文档。 这是有免费试用额度的付费服务：注册赠送 100 积分，可导出一级评论的 CSV；回复和 Excel 格式需要订阅。一级评论与回复共用所设的导出上限，能拿到多少内容取决于公开视频当前可见的数据，不保证抓全。

projects.title: 【工具自荐】HyperCopy：Hyperliquid 交易员分析、监控与自动跟单工具，支持 Web 和 App
projects.author: ganondorf789
projects.summary: 大家好，我自己平时很喜欢炒股和研究交易，也会关注加密货币、美股、黄金、原油这些市场。 平时使用各大交易所的跟单功能时，我发现热门交易员经常有跟单名额限制，平台展示的数据也不够完整，很难真正看清交易员的长期表现、持仓风格和风险；跟单产生收益后，通常还需要给带单员分润。 这些限制让我一直觉得不够自由，也是我后来决定开发 HyperCopy 的主要原因。 所以我开发了 HyperCopy ，希望把“发现交易员—分析表现—监控动态—执行跟单”放进一个产品里。 主要功能有： 发现和筛选交易员 可以根据盈亏、收益率、胜率、最大回撤、夏普比率、持仓方向、杠杆和交易频率等指标筛选交易员，尽量避免只看短期收益排行榜就盲目跟单。 查看交易员历史表现 支持查看当前持仓、最近成交、历史交易、盈亏曲线、仓位分布和风险指标，先了解交易风格，再决定是否跟单。 自动跟单和立即跟单 可以指定交易员自动跟单，也可以看到实时持仓后手动选择立即跟单。开仓后还能根据设置继续跟随加仓、减仓和平仓。 仓位与风险控制 支持按资产比例、仓位比例或固定金额跟单，并可设置止盈止损、最大仓位、滑点保护和保证金保护等参数。不同市场的具体选项会根据交易账户和品种有所区别。 行情和账户监控 可以关注交易员或账户的持仓变化、开平仓动态和风险变化，并接收相应通知。HyperCopy 同时支持 Web 和 APP ，两端账户、监控列表和跟单配置互通，都可以直接查看和管理跟单。 速度方面，目前在线实测，从捕获目标交易员的成交或仓位变化，到跟单订单提交，通常约为 1–2 秒。 体验地址： Web： App 下载： 这是我自己因为喜欢交易而开发的产品，目前仍在持续迭代，也包含部分付费功能。跟单不代表稳赚，建议先观察策略，并用小资金测试。 界面截图：

projects.title: Show HN: Fluidify – A wiki of the industrial world being built (post-2026)
projects.author: gts_nesov
projects.summary: I built a system with the objective of mapping all the major announced infrastructure and industrial projects around the world. The vast majority of listed projects are expected to become operational after 2026. As you would expect, I used some agents to fill in the map, but for several reasons, some information may not be up to date or as accurate as it could be. The agents provide the initial “breadth,” while the idea is for the community to improve the accuracy over time with what they know: a new source URL, a correction, or a time-stamped picture from the ground. I see several use cases here: - finding a job where industrial activity is getting stronger - finding new logistics opportunities for a freight forwarder, as new industrial plants generate new recurring freight demand - helping select a future site in an emerging industrial cluster - detecting future real estate opportunities where the market hasn’t fully priced in I also see Fluidify as a way to explore beyond the places and projects you would normally think to search for. Most discovery starts with a location, company, or market you already know. On Fluidify, you can simply move across the map and discover industrial activity somewhere you were not looking: a new factory, an emerging cluster, or a region attracting several large investments at once. That can lead to opportunities you would never have thought to search for in the first place. As I invested my own money to build this, contractor data is not available for every project. Mapping and verifying contractors globally would simply be too expensive for me to do alone at this stage. You can message me (email in "About" on the website at the bottom), I’d be glad to show you the data behind the "hidden" tabs.

projects.summary: I developed this application because in my professional contracting the same pattern of problems came up client after client, how much of the microcontroller or flash is used, and can we do [FEATURE] with what we have. As an embedded engineer the output of arm-none-eabi-size and a spreadsheet tells me the story, but an email or a slide for the client doesn't do it. Another motivator for this project was why not make today look like the future of the movies! You watch tech action movies and there is 3D rotation views of processors, or circuits as holograms right in front of you, or animations of zooming through networks. These movie effects are designed for the exact same thing professional engineers want, to get the info across in an instant to people who don’t know the details. The action hero needs to show the mega-gigatron reactor is almost full, so the green-yellow-red bar graph is almost full, spinning and blinking red with a flashing warning sign suggesting impending doom! While in reality the stakes are less dramatic than that, imagine if the information on how full a system is was conveyed to a PM or VP in the same way? That's the goal of this project, give the engineer the tool to show the boss the details graphically, and make it look good. It's free to use. projects.title: Show HN: SolidPing — open-source uptime monitoring, agents inside your network
projects.author: fclairamb
projects.summary: SolidPing is a single Go binary, AGPL-3.0 — 40 check types, status pages, incidents, on-call escalation, and sub-minute intervals that aren't paywalled. I loved Better Stack, and then the free plan kept getting thinner. What finally pushed me over: incidents used to get one Slack thread each, so an outage lived in one conversation instead of a stream of disconnected messages. That went away. I wanted it back, so I built my own. The part I'd most like torn apart is the agents. You run one inside the network you want watched and it dials out over a WebSocket, so there's no inbound port and no firewall hole. On first start it generates its own keypairs and keeps the private halves — Ed25519 for identity, an X25519 (age) recipient that the server seals check credentials to. So the credentials for a private check are encrypted for that agent, and the server storing them can't read them. All of it is open source: the agents, WhatsApp alerts, SSO, every check type. Nothing held back for a hosted edition. Self-hosting is genuinely easy, and I depend on it, https://status.solidping.io is a second SolidPing running on fly.io that watches the cluster hosting the first one. A monitor that lives inside what it monitors isn't a monitor. I've maintained a small Go FTP server library for 10 years (github.com/fclairamb/ftpserverlib), so open source isn't a marketing decision here. Demo, no signup: https://solidping.io/demo Source: https://github.com/fclairamb/solidping What I want is UX feedback and missing features — where the interface gets in your way, what you went looking for and couldn't find, what would have to exist before you'd run this instead of what you run now. Please be blunt. "Nice project" teaches me nothing.

projects.title: Show HN: Mutt-like mail client with terminal HTML+img, MCP, CRM & scheduled mail
projects.author: rjzzleep
projects.summary: For the past few weeks I've been working on my mail client which is behaviorally based on neomutt, but it has a unified inbox/archive/etc. which is based on a notmuch backend. neomutt was a big pain for me to use with tag based email handling, and it's really hard to get it setup and working mail moving, when using a tag based workflow. I still found a bug in maildir flag handling by two days ago, so it turns out I underestimated all the corner cases that exist, but it should be good now. There is a setup function that sets up fcc and the folder structure per account. It does things such as schedule mail with NLP. It's fully async, it's tabbed, and because the HTML client(which supports images in the terminal) is fully integrated, when you use the MCP, it converts the HTML into useful text rather than feeding full HTML. It validates s/mime, but i didn't dare implementing gpg support it. There is a lua plugin example for using external file browsers like yazi for attachment selection. It also has a CRM queue that can be used to process new contacts with a pluggable api backend(only hubspot for now). Two things that are still in flux, which is why you would probably consider this alpha software is the config structure. For example I changed the mcp config to be per account permissions, rather than simple permissions, so I can gate each account. There is still a lot to do make this production quality, but I use it as a daily driver now. https://github.com/fishman/notmutt https://fishman.github.io/notmutt/

projects.author: markogg
projects.summary: Hi! My name is Marko, and I'm a developer (primarily backend) who loves building stuff. I've been trying to solve a problem of scattered operational context across Slack threads, tickets, meetings, etc. (my way)... The idea of Trailogs is to be a central event-based history, where each event (log) has structure around it, like categorization, ownership, etc... It has an exploration page, which is basically an AI chat where you can ask questions about what is happening in the company, why a certain decision was made, what is going on with a specific customer, who was responsible for a certain thing, etc... I realized that "what should I ask?" could be a problem, so the chat gives you suggestions based on your role in the team and interests. So if you are a developer, you could get a suggestion to ask about a certain deployment/feature release from today. If you are in sales, you'll get a suggestion to ask about negotiations that happened today with a certain customer. The chat is currently powered by OpenAI. Now, I understand the privacy concerns and sensitivity of the data, so I'm planning an implementation with a self-hosted LLM, or the possibility for users to use their own LLM. I was thinking about how to reduce the friction so teams don't have to manually log stuff every time, so, for now, I implemented the possibility to integrate through an API and webhooks (incoming, outgoing). Also, since a lot of team conversations happen in Slack, I've built a Slack integration so you can ask questions directly from Slack or ask it to draft a log based on what was discussed in a thread. The app is functional and can be tried. It has a registration form, but I made it possible to just continue with a demo account, so you don't have to leave any personal information if you don't want to, and you can quickly get straight to the demo workspace. Poke around, let me know what you think. :)

projects.title: Show HN: Revliu – Multi-touch attribution from acquisition to revenue
projects.author: TychiqueY
projects.summary: I’m a founder and I just built RevliI’m a founder and I just built Revliu. After building several products, I always wanted to understand how my customers were actually finding me. Which campaign brought them in, which source they came from, and what their full journey looked like. There are already tools for this, but one problem I kept running into is that they often stop at first touch or last touch. That’s why I built Revliu around multi-touch attribution and the full customer journey. As soon as someone lands on your website, Revliu gives them an anonymous ID and starts tracking their journey. Once they sign up, that journey can be connected to the actual customer. From there, you can see if they’re on a trial, how often they come back, how many sessions they open, and eventually when they pay. For me, this also makes it easier to talk to that user and understand why they decided to move forward at that specific moment. Today, Revliu tracks acquisition sources, returning visitors, sessions, touchpoints, and revenue. Instead of just knowing that a campaign got a certain number of impressions, I want to know how much money it actually brought in. Impressions are not really what I care about. The app itself is pretty simple. The main page gives you an overview of revenue by source. Traffic shows visitors, their journey, and their sessions. Campaigns shows the acquisition funnel. For a SaaS, that can be visitor → lead → trial → paying customer. For an online store, it can simply be acquisition → purchase. Customers lets you look at each customer individually, see their touchpoints, where they came from, their journey, and when they bought. The technical side is simple in principle. It starts with an anonymous visitor who gets an ID. We keep track of their visits and touchpoints. When they sign up, that anonymous journey is connected to the customer. Stripe is connected as well, so when the customer pays, the revenue can be linked back to the same journey. The goal is basically to connect acquisition → visits → signup → customer → revenue. Right now, the app is still in its first phase. I haven’t built all the integrations I want yet. What I want to build next is something that does more than just show data. If someone leaves their email but never finishes signing up, comes back several times without buying, or shows real interest without converting, I want to use that information to try to recover that potential customer. The idea would be to reach them again by email or, depending on the integrations, through other channels like LinkedIn. That’s why I still see the app as limited today. I first want to test this attribution part and see if there’s real traction around the problem before building everything else. The part I’m really interested in for the future is revenue recovery. By combining it with AI, the goal would be to adapt to different customers, understand which ones are hesitating, and do more than just display data. I want the data to actually do something inside the product. And I’d really like to know how you’re handling this today. Coding has become much easier than it used to be, but the difference between a good product that sells and a good product nobody uses often comes down to marketing and distribution. I’d really like your feedback on Revliu, the way I’m approaching the problem, and what you would do differently.

projects.title: 【开源自荐】适合中国宝宝体质的 AI 求职助手：个性画像→BOSS爬虫→人岗匹配→可视化分析
projects.author: ZhishaBai-web

github.name: ZhishaBai-web/help-you-find-job
github.description: 本项目是一套适合中国宝宝体质的 AI 求职助手系统，采用 Python、Streamlit、LangChain、RAG、Web 自动化及数据分析等技术，构建“用户画像—职业规划—岗位采集—人岗匹配—数据分析”的一体化求职辅助流程。系统能够基于用户简历与求职偏好生成结构化职业画像，自动采集并处理招聘岗位信息，利用 RAG 与 LLM 从能力、职责、发展、背景、潜力等维度进行智能匹配与评分，并通过数据可视化展示岗位市场及匹配结果，从而帮助求职者降低岗位筛选成本，提升决策效率。

projects.summary: 1. 项目地址 项目仓库： 线上体验： 视频演示： 2. 项目亮点 本项目是目前 GitHub 上较少见的覆盖 “用户画像—职业规划—岗位采集—人岗匹配—数据分析” 完整流程的纯 Python 项目。 对用户进行画像分析时，在考虑用户简历的基础上，还考虑了用户的性格特点。 各阶段分析结果，均可查、可复制、可下载，具有较高的可观察性和可控性。 3. 项目展示 3.1 工作喵 🐱 上传简历 + 回答 15 个偏好问题，生成用户画像、职业报告、岗位检索词，也可以直接和 AI 聊求职。 3.2 爬虫喵 🕷️ 使用 DrissionPage 自动采集招聘岗位信息，检索词和筛选条件都可以自己设置。 3.3 分析喵 📊 岗位少的话，直接交给 LLM 分析；岗位多的话，先用 RAG 筛出相关性最高的 50 个，再让 LLM 做详细的人岗匹配。 3.4 工具喵 🛠️ 合并岗位、查看 TOP 岗位、分析单/全岗位、数据可视化，都可以在这里实现。 4. 注意事项 本项目仅用于学习、研究与技术交流，请勿用于任何违法或违规用途。 线上 Demo 暂不支持爬虫功能，建议根据视频教程进行本地部署。 AI 生成的分析结果仅供参考，请结合实际情况进行判断。

projects.title: Show HN: Relay – an update after three years on anonymous team check-ins
projects.author: techdiff
projects.summary: Three years ago I posted our product Signals here: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=34405962 It’s rebranded to Relay now. Same idea-ish. We’ve cut back a lot but leaned right into the anonymity aspect for staff. We believe that as long as we protect the ability of the team to have a voice without negative consequences, then management gets more accurate data to act on. And also that it’s managements role to listen and respond to the commentary, even if just to acknowledge it. We have definitely taken a hard path on this. The product requires strong management or team leads who aren’t afraid of criticism … funnily enough, that doesn’t make it easily saleable. But the businesses that are using it, and responding weekly to their teams concerns, do see a growth in trust and engagement. That lowers staff churn, increases institutional knowledge, etc. etc. Additionally - we’re an AUS based business where state laws on psychosocial safety are quite strict - we actually meet the reporting, recording and response requirements for that legislation. We’ve made loads of product improvements - AI generated summaries that keep context on the clients over time, easier account sign ups and logins, simpler pricing, better dashboards and an increase in anonymity through how we collect responses. Over the last three years we have learnt that we are not sales people. It’s our single biggest challenge. We’re just not good at it. So that’s something we’re trying to solve. It’s free to sign up and start using it. We’d love any and all feedback - the last time we posted was super valuable and I really appreciated everyones feedback.

projects.title: Show HN: SiteTell: finds the areas of your site that read as AI-generic
projects.author: NotGeorgeHere
projects.summary: Hey everyone, I built this product called SiteTell. You put in your website url, it returns a list of all of the things across the site that get flagged as likely to be AI-written/AI-generic. It works against a curated rule set (which will obviously get updated as AI models update and evolve) and then you can fix these issues and get a PDF/CSV/JSON file that you can download to either take the suggested fixes yourself and apply them, or use the CSV/JSON file to drop into your agent for it to fix autonomously within minutes. I actually ran it through my first copy of SiteTell and my rule set gave me an overall score of 6/100. Woops. Google updated its core rules in February 2026. The important thing to note is that it does not punish AI-written content. It instead punishes thin content, or generic content. The stuff that AI will typically write if you don't go and edit it after. SiteTell can fix this by taking these generic, common issues such as stock AI openers (think 'in today's fast paced world'), AI vocabulary (see 'seamlessly integrates') or far more subtle things that once you notice, you see everywhere. For example, consecutive paragraphs within 8 or so words of the same length. The other way I think SiteTell helps is through trust. Increasingly if you go to a landing page, or even a whole site, that reads generically and has the typical AI tells (em-dashes etc...) it instantly loses some amount of intangible trust with the customer which could be costing you customers if you run a site with a lot of written copy. SiteTell also aims to fix this. The rule set is really the main product in my opinion. It's about 200 rules covering vocabulary, sentence structure, hedging, and some layout patterns, built from public slop-word lists, a corpus diff against pre-2022 marketing copy, and a lot of manual tuning against real sites. False positives are the hard part, particularly with technical writing where precise language reads as formulaic. Because of the false positive situation, if a user chooses to go through with the fixes they can pick and choose what parts actually need fixing. The customer gets granular control and gets to essentially remove the false positives before the fix stage. Detection is pure regex and heuristics, so scanning is free and needs no signup. Rewrites cost money because they hit an API, so those are paid. Stack is Next.js, Supabase, Gemini Flash for the rewrites only.

projects.summary: 【开源自荐】Resume Builder：让 AI agent 像聊天一样陪你写简历 我是 Resume Builder 的开发者，自荐一个开源项目：Resume Builder。 传统 AI 简历工具，通常是“填表 → AI 优化 → 导出”。用户输入被局限在表单里，AI 也只能在平台规则内帮你改，改完就结束了，讨论、口径、红线都留不下来。 Resume Builder 换了一种方式：你下载项目，在豆包、Codex、DSH 这类 AI agent 里加载 AGENTS.md，然后直接聊天，AI 会像一位简历顾问一样，陪你一块一块改。 和在线 AI 简历工具不同，这不是 SaaS，而是本地开源项目：用户下载后在自己的 AI agent 里加载，数据是本地 YAML，并带有 reference 记忆区和 HTML 中间产物。 特点： 内容全部是本地 YAML，不需要懂 YAML，AI 负责写 每个 YAML 末尾有 reference 记忆区：用户原话、口径、红线、待确认事项都记在这里，构建时自动截断，不会进入最终简历 一个 YAML 一个 YAML 讨论修改，不一次性生成整份简历 中间产物是 HTML，AI 可以直接读 HTML/CSS：用户说“超页了”“不要红色”，AI 能直接定位并修改 一份标准简历可以复制成多个岗位 JD 定制版本 一键导出 HTML / PDF / 长图 / 分页 PNG 开源、本地、无账号，数据在自己手里 快速体验： bash git clone cd resume-builder python -m pip install -r requirements.txt python make.py build --person demo 打开 output/demo-/demo-.html 就能看到效果。 项目还很新，我更想分享的不是“又一个简历生成器”，而是“简历不应该靠填表，应该靠聊天”这个想法。

projects.title: Show HN: I audited my SEC pipeline, found 82.7% of split adjustments were wrong
projects.author: Loris_jk
projects.summary: Hello HN! I built a pipeline which fetches SEC EDGAR 10k and 10qs for more than 600 companies, maps xbrl-tags onto around 35 financial concepts and computes growth- , fundamental- and valuation-multiples (prices provided by yfinance). This project originated bc I wanted clean, non-third-party financial data in order to judge a trading thesis of mine. I could not find any app providing such data (for free), let alone being open source. Turns out there are no data providers because xbrl of 10ks and 10qs SUCKS(!!!!). It is messy, unregulated and devastated. Its the wild west of finance. A project like this was 5 years ago not possible, at least not with less than ~1000 people. Thats because of the nature of xbrl-tags. Since they are unregulated, a certain xbrl-tag could fit perfectly for a certain company, while providing nothing, only a partial amount, or complete garbage for another company. You would have to iterate through every financial statement ever relesed by a company, searching every tag possbile, comparing, once found, a tag and constantly checking, once more companies are added to the obserable universe, if the tag also produces meaningfull data for those new companies. As I said, unmanagable task. Except for LLMs. I used Anthropics Claude Fable 5 mostly, giving strict, non-regression focused tag research tasks, constantly letting it iterate through the entire ticker universe, searching and comparing tags. And it worked. It took me around 3 weeks just to produce wrong data, manually searching for a ticker universe of 3 (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA). Now this pipeline produces correct, cleaned data (more on that later) for more than 600 companies. That was just the main problem tho. Notable problems taht also had to be fixed: -companies tagging everything as fy ull year; -cash flow being filed cumulative; -q4 is never filed; -a quarter isnt always the same length; tag changing by a company; -STOCK SPLITS (god i hate them); -companies reporting wrong (a few 0s more for example); Still got a lot of work to do, UI and UX are...rudimentary. Appreciate any feedback/critics. Thanks for taking your time reading this. repo link: https://github.com/lorisjk/stock_valuator

projects.author: yoyao
projects.summary: Hi HN! I'm an SEO and AI search consultant. I've spent years creating topical maps and content strategies for brands and that led me to building Floyi. I’ve seen over the years, long before AI-generated content, how content strategies started with individual keywords and disconnected article ideas. Teams published more, but organic traffic stalled and sometimes declined because the content focus was fragmented. That’s why I always start by defining the brand, what it wants to be known for, and their buyers’ needs. Then I turn that context into topical research, a topical map, and a content publishing plan. The problem I kept having was keeping the brand’s context across the separate tools, documents, and spreadsheets throughout the workflow. By the time you were ready to start a brief or writing, you had to remember to find the brand and writing guidelines first to ensure the brand’s voice was intact. I built Floyi to keep the process in one workflow, carrying brand/audience context from research to mapping to content briefs to articles. You can try it here for free: https://app.floyi.com/ I would appreciate feedback on improvements, especially where the workflow feels fragmented.

projects.title: Show HN: OctoLoops – automated marketing for indie devs
projects.author: davedx
projects.summary: Hi HN! This is my latest side hustle, OctoLoops: an app to help indie devs and SMEs find paying customers for their business. I first started building OctoLoops around 2 months ago because so many of my own projects, big and small, had failed or petered out from lack of users and the valuable feedback that comes with them. When I started seriously digging, I found that distribution is one heck of a rabbit hole. The more I read, the more I found how much I didn't know. But I wanted to learn - and I really wanted to _apply_ that learning too, to all my new projects, in a repeatable, autonomous-as-possible way. What better way to implement this plan than building a distribution app? The idea was supposedly simple: implement a handful of "agentic loops" that anyone could easily run, in a web UI - no downloads or installing Claude Code, no complexity, human stays in the loop. A simple agentic harness in the browser with some superpowers to let it do its job. I launched it quite soon after, and immediately started dogfooding, running the Community Loop. It found threads across Reddit from all those builders who'd made something cool, but were now at a loss when it came to finding and acquiring users. It drafted replies for me and gave a "spam risk", because yes - many kinds of marketing and sales walk a fine line between signal and blatant spam - and I started working the loops. Often I'd edit or write the replies myself; sometimes I'd remove the OctoLoops mention from the message. It worked. I now have ~50 users, including one from a post-revenue B2B startup interested in using the Outbound loop. But there have been significant challenges already that I want to be open about here, in the hope that it helps other public builders. 1. Activation. This is currently my #1 pain point. My Community loops work - I can get people to sign up, enter their email, and I know there's even some buying intent. But people often log in once, then don't use the app. I've reached out to users, and they've said it's partly just that they don't want to post their app in communities they don't yet feel a real part of. Resistance to being rude or spammy, imposter syndrome - anyone who's done any marketing can identify. I'm trying to solve some of the issues of activation by building a more streamlined, less cluttered UX, but I'm not sure how to motivate people to really use the app in earnest. Maybe it's missing evidence of outcomes? Video tutorials? 2. Product focus. While researching competitors, what I notice most have in common is they focus on _one thing_: automated outbound; automated advertising; keyword monitoring. Not many people seem to be trying to make a fully autonomous omnichannel GTM agent, because that's too much. I decided to hide most of the channels I'd built already behind UI so users focus on community outreach and outbound sales. It's too early to say if that's the right call, and I know I'm still following an omnichannel strategy for OctoLoops itself. 3. Prioritising. I'm sure everyone says this, but: content strategy; SEO; socials; dogfooding... trying to talk to users, to understand why I'm not yet solving their problems and delivering them the outcomes they want. Attempting to keep my potential corporate customer in the funnel. Implementing new features - but which ones? And keeping up with the _insane pace_ of agentic apps and AI at large: so much is happening right now, hype and BS is everywhere, sometimes it's hard to know what's real. So that's where I'm at, 2 months down the line. It's already been a fun journey. Any questions I'm happy to answer. Criticism is welcome too - I recognize some will view this as contributing to the already high volume of spam and slop out there, but that's honestly a balance I'm trying to find, and I'd love to hear opinions on how people should do sales and marketing in 2026 without driving people crazy.

github.name: dashloom-dev/dashloom
github.description: Dashloom is an open-source product intelligence platform for people operating one or many digital products. It combines dashboards, connected business data, specialized AI agents, scheduled reports, and action tracking.

projects.summary: 一个独立开发者，小型SaaS团队，或者代理运营团队可用的 AI情报系统。 以上这些角色大部分应该都会开发和运营十几个甚至几十个产品。这些产品的各种数据分散在分析工具、支付平台、代码仓库和云基础设施中，每次要把所有数据整体过一次，要经历很长的时间，如果想让AI辅助帮忙把数据整理一遍，还得花时间花心思挨个导出再丢给AI做分析，非常麻烦。 这就是我遇到的问题和痛点。于是我花了很长时间给自己搞了一个系统来解决这些问题，并且慢慢的打磨了很长时间，最近有朋友也有类似的痛点，于是我又花了一段时间，把这个项目开源了，并给这个项目命名为 Dashloom。 Dashloom 会把上述多个数据源的数据标准化到统一的证据层，然后 Dashloom Agent 先通过确定性指标和信号雷达找出值得关注的变化，再让你自己的 OpenAI 兼容模型进行分析，生成带证据引用的洞察、行动建议和定期报告。 又可以作为统一的数据大盘查看和分析数据，又可以通过 Agent 的能力为数据提供分析洞察，行动建议，定期报告，并且还能通过安装各种skill来丰富agent的能力。 支持多个产品的数据隔离，并提供以下几种预设场景的 agent 能力： 独立开发者 SaaS 收入 SEO 增长 Cloudflare 运维 客户报告 Agent 的结论需要引用实际证据，不会把相关性直接描述为因果关系。 开源版本为完全自部署系统，自己部署，接入自己的数据，使用自己的API，没有任何隐私泄露问题。可以根据自己的实际需要来让codex或者cc code帮自己调整功能或者进行二次开发。 目前支持的数据源包括： 产品与增长： Google Analytics、Google Search Console、Bing Master 收入与支付： Stripe、Lemon Squeezy、Creem、Polar、Paddle 或者导入自己数据库中的自定义收入数据（这样可以覆盖所有支付渠道） 开发与部署： GitHub、Vercel Cloudflare： Workers、Pages、Queues、R2 数据库与后端： Supabase、Cloudflare D1 自定义数据： Custom REST、手动指标导入、开放摄取 API、TypeScript SDK 和 Connector Worker 支持OAuth的平台可以简单配置一下一键接入，有些需要自己搞一下变量和密钥。 开源项目地址和介绍 在线cloud版本（还没完善好，免费试用，在关联Google数据提示未认证的位置点击高级，信任即可）：

projects.title: Show HN: Keeplea – photograph everything you want to remember
projects.author: BrainQuanta
projects.summary: At some point I noticed how many photos I take just to remember something, to come back to it later, when I need it. The packaging of a product I liked, a notice on the door of some government place, small paper documents, screenshots of something that felt important at the time. Well, even the wiring inside the walls during a renovation, photographed "for the future". All of it lands in the photo gallery next to the "real" photos, and then you almost never come back to any of it, because finding one specific thing in that random stream is just not realistic. Yes, modern mobile OSes categorize photos automatically and let you search the text on them. But the categorization is primitive, like "mountains", "documents", "screenshots", and the thing you're looking for isn't always written on the photo. The native photo gallery will never find me that photo of the wiring behind the kitchen wall. There's no text on it, and "wiring" is not a category. So the idea was a mobile app where all these utility photos go, and I don't have to maintain them in any way - automatic categorization, with semantic search on top. Give it a try and let me know what you think: Website: https://keeplea.app Get the app: https://get.keeplea.app So far it's all pretty hard. No users yet - an app like this has low "search" potential, nobody types this problem into a store search box. But I'll keep trying, as they say. Under the hood: KMP, native UI, Firebase, Gemini, Firestore vector search. P.S. Let me say it right away: this app wasn't vibecoded over the weekend, as people like to put it these days. Honestly, I hate the term "vibecoding". It downplays the weeks and months that go into thinking through the idea, the architecture, the experiments, the design, the marketing, etc. The fact that you use AI agents while building doesn't mean you slapped something together and spat it into production. Although, true, plenty of people nowadays do exactly that. Well, not me

You'd spend the day measuring up jobs and talking to customers, then get home tired and realise you've still got a load of quotes to write. That was the reason I started building Snapquo. If you've got a bigger quote to work on, you can sit at a computer and do it there. The basic idea is pretty simple. Get the quote done, send it to the customer, let them accept and sign it, take a deposit if you want to, and then turn it into an invoice. It now has things like: • Quotes you can build quickly from your phone • Photos and optional extras • Customer acceptance and signatures • Deposits • Automatic quote follow-ups • Quote-open tracking • Saved prices • Quote to invoice • Online payments • Pipeline and win/loss tracking • iPhone, Android and web apps • Free tools for things like VAT, CIS, Day rate calculator, Invoice generator and a lot more. I have deliberately tried not to turn it into another massive CRM with loads of features that a small trade business probably doesn't need. I wanted something I would have actually used when I was on the tools. I'd genuinely like to hear your feedback. Thanks :)

projects.author: chen2he
projects.summary: Apolu 追踪你自己的 App 在全球 App Store 的榜单排名。 App Store 只让开发者看到自己所在的那一个国家/地区，而全世界有 175 个。三个平台、26 个分类、免费榜和付费榜加起来是两万多张实时榜单，Apple 没有任何接口能回答「我的 App 现在排第几」——只能有人一直抓、一直记着。Apolu 做的就是这件事：读 Apple 的榜单页面（每张 200 名），30 个大市场每小时一次，其余每四小时一次。 排名：175 个国家/地区 × iPhone/iPad/Mac × 免费榜/付费榜，带历史曲线 提醒：新进入一个国家、冲进前十、单次上升二十名这类值得看一眼的变化，不是每日流水账 评论：所有国家的新评论汇进一个收件箱，低分优先，可以直接在 App 内回复 收入：用你自己创建的 App Store Connect API 密钥读你自己的销售报表——真实的开发者分成，按日按国家，不是第三方估算模型 界面 13 种语言，iPhone / iPad / Mac / Apple Watch / 小组件 主屏小组件：在榜国家与各自名次、当日收入、待回复评论。 上榜之后可以生成一张战绩海报，图片或短视频，App 内所有语言都支持。 免费可以追踪任意数量的 App，看到所有市场的前 25 名，榜单随便浏览；PRO（$6.99/月、$39.99/年、$79.99 买断）解锁完整前 100 名、历史、提醒、评论回复和收入。排名数据完全不需要登录，只有评论和收入需要授权。 顺便说个做的时候才发现的事：apps.apple.com 链接里的国家码只是提示，不是指令——Apple 按请求来源判定 storefront，所以你在自己电脑上打开「其他国家」的商品页，看到的其实还是本国的。想知道自己在别的市场排第几，靠手动查是查不出来的。 先说清楚没有的：关键词排名和 ASO 建议都没做；也不估算任何 App（包括竞品）的下载量和收入。App 闭源。 这是作者本人自荐。

projects.title: Show HN: Python Static Site Generator for Small Businesses
projects.author: marking-time
projects.summary: A static site generator for small web based store front for a brick and mortar store. It uses a local data store: FOSS This software is intended to fill the gap between a "full" frontend/backend solution and a simple static front end site in that it employs local data stores to create a static website that can be easily updated by the store owner. Features: - A python script run by the user that accesses a local CSV data store and builds a static html page. This greatly reduces complexity while still giving the user the ability to modify the data. - It is run by executing a python script from the command line. - After the initial html file is built, the user will use the hosting provider's website to upload the html file to the hosting server. - The script is simple enough that an beginning/intermediate python/html dev can update the script, data store and resulting index.html file without additional research or support. Using this software should be within ability range of a superuser. - This software and its output is written as simply as possible to allow for customization as needed. + It uses no additional frameworks, just native html/CSS. + It uses no libraries not included in standard python. + No JavaScript is used. The output is simple html/CSS. All the CSS is embedded in the html file to make it easier to manage the files. Only the resulting index.html file needs to be uploaded to the hosting server. + It uses common spreadsheet software to manage the data for both the Store Information and the products to be listed. - This software is Free and Open Source Software(FOSS) and can be edited by the user or their agent. Suitability: This software is suitable to the small store owner that is looking to move into online sales/marketing, but doesn't want to commit to a large development project or ongoing costs. It can be advertised using a QR code linking to the hosting provider. This eliminates the need for a domain name. Possible Uses: - Small brick and mortar stores - SwapMeet vendors - Yard sales

projects.title: Show HN: The AI agent that works inside the apps you use
projects.author: mej2020
projects.summary: I'm Mitchell, the founder at Lava. The short version: it's a desktop app that puts an agent next to the apps you're already logged in to, and it does the work through a direct connection to each app instead of driving a browser. You describe a task, it reads your real data, builds a plan, and executes it. Scoped permissions: reads run freely, but writes, sends, deletes, and payments need your approval. A concrete one: you say "follow up with everyone from last week's demos" and it reads your CRM and your calendar, drafts the emails in Gmail, and posts the summary in Slack. That's one conversation, not four tabs. There are 200+ providers connected today, covering all the apps your team already uses, so the same shape works for whatever your stack actually is. Why a direct connection and not browser automation: we started with a browser agent and it was miserable. Every time a site updated its layout, something broke. It was slow, and there was no clean way to tell the user what was about to happen. A direct connection to each app means every step is a specific action with known inputs, which is what makes the approval screen possible at all. The tradeoff: we only support what an app makes available through its connection, and we had to build a connector per app instead of getting everything for free. What makes this different from the alternatives: you don't need an engineering team to set up a workflow. You describe what you want in plain language and the agent plans and executes it. You can switch between AI models, so you're not locked into one provider. For apps that don't have a connector yet, Lava can also work through your open browser tabs, so the agent isn't limited to what has a connector. And any conversation can become a scheduled routine that runs on its own. To be clear: the download is free, but the agent runs on credits or a subscription. You need an account for the agent to work. The part I'd most like feedback on is the permission model. Permission fatigue is a real problem and there's been a lot of discussion on HN about it. We use scoped permissions with three modes: always ask, ask before sending (the default: reads run freely, anything that writes, sends, deletes or pays stops and asks), and never ask. The default is the safe one and also the annoying one. The approval gate is also what stops a prompt-injected agent from doing something you didn't ask for. If every write needs your sign-off, the attack surface shrinks. Scheduled routines run without a prompt because nobody is there to answer, and I'm not fully comfortable with that asymmetry. If you've shipped something in this shape, I'd like to hear where you landed. Practical notes: direct download for macOS and Windows. The build is signed and notarized. Happy to trade notes with anyone building agents that touch real user accounts.

projects.title: Show HN: Ifso – A personal finance simulator for major life decisions
projects.author: timer_interrupt
projects.summary: Hello all! Ifso is a personal finance simulator that takes all of your various accounts (like taxable brokerages, retirement accounts, loans, etc) and various life events (like income changes, retirement, purchasing a home, increasing principal contributions to your home mortgage, etc.) and plays it out year by year for you. The simulation engine underneath the hood handles all of the tax math, capital gains math, investment growth rates, home appreciation, vehicle depreciation, loan amortization, and more. You can then create multiple scenarios by duplicating an existing one or creating a fresh new one, and compare two scenarios side by side, helping you understand how big decisions would affect your overall financial wellbeing and goals. This project started off as something I wanted to use myself. I didn't really find a lot of the one-off calculators helpful since they don't take all of the other factors in my finances into account, and they also don't allow flexibility in what you can get out of it. For example, if I wanted to drop investment contributions for a few years and then resume later, a typical investment calculator doesn't allow for that level of granularity. On the other hand, there were a few solutions available out there that did financial simulations (and they're definitely useful, much respect for them), but they felt a bit over-complicated trying to get off the ground. Additionally, they were too pricey for me, and their free tiers don't necessarily let you save your simulations, which I found frustrating. I also had a bit of a hard time with decision making since it didn't feel like comparing scenarios was a first-class citizen feature. That's what led me to start building a simulator myself, I wanted something that felt more intuitive for me and actually catered towards decision making. I wanted to see, for example, what would happen if I sold my house in a few years versus renting it out (I simulate rental properties in Ifso as well). How do both of those scenarios play out if I get a promotion this year and also decide to upgrade my wife's car? Some things to note about Ifso: - The free tier currently gives you access to the entire simulation engine and one saved scenario. Your scenarios are saved, so it persists across sessions/devices. - The paid tier is $9/mo or $69/year (dropped down to $59/yr for the first 100 users, and this price is locked in until you cancel). This includes everything in the free tier + unlocks building multiple scenarios and comparing them side by side + Monte Carlo simulations. - The app is US-specific as of now, if there's demand for supporting other locations I can always look into it. - There's a number of account types and events that you can configure, and I'm constantly working on adding more. I ultimately want this to be as helpful and dynamic as possible, while remaining approachable and as intuitive as possible. - There's no bank or account linking, so everything is manual input. You can export your data and you can also delete your account altogether. Data is never shared or sold. - Sign-in is done via Google OAuth so your setup persists across sessions and devices. There is a short demo video on the site in case you want to see what things look like before signing in. Let me know what you think! In particular, I want to make sure that the overall UX and UI is intuitive. My first set of users had given me feedback that helped me improve the UX, UI, and onboarding flow. If there's parts of the UX that work for you, and other parts that you find unintuitive, please be sure to share. Things make sense to me as I'm building it out, but ultimately it's what you guys think that matters. If there's other features, account or event types, etc. that you think would be valuable, please share that as well!

projects.title: Samyama Graph: a Rust graph database with built-in vector search
projects.author: HimadriSur
projects.summary: Project URL Category Rust Project Title A Rust graph database with built-in vector search Project Description A graph database written in Rust that runs OpenCypher queries and vector search in a single engine. Setup is one docker pull, and it ships 11 case studies built from public data - cricket, IMDB, court judgments - so you can run real queries on day one. Highlights Most projects in this space make you run two systems: a graph database for relationships and a vector store for embeddings, kept in sync by your own code. Samyama Graph runs OpenCypher traversal and HNSW vector search in one process, so a "who is connected to whom" query and a "what is similar to this" query hit the same engine and the same data. It is also easy to start, which matters more than the architecture for anyone trying it out. One docker pull from a public registry - no account, no signup, no sales call - and the casestudies directory has 11 datasets that rebuild themselves from public sources: cricket ball-by-ball records, IMDB, Indian Supreme Court judgments, drug interactions, protein pathways. Each one ships its loader and its queries, so you can go from empty database to a real answer in an evening. Apache-2.0, written in Rust, 14 graph algorithms. The benchmark page publishes its own unflattering results, including two runs of the same binary that differed by 24%. Example Code markdown // Which bowler has dismissed which batsman most often? // 36,619 nodes and 1,392,017 edges of ball-by-ball cricket data. MATCH (bowler:Player)-[d:DISMISSED]->(batsman:Player) RETURN bowler.name, batsman.name, count(d) AS times ORDER BY times DESC LIMIT 5 Screenshots or Demo Videos A one-minute demo of Claude querying six of these knowledge graphs over MCP, picking the server and writing the Cypher itself: The eleven case studies, each with its loader and queries:
